title: Oncall handoff draft - Olivia Hu
content:
TL;DR:
- Night shift: 03/03 -> 03/04. Major noisy incident with inference-worker pool (pool-3) causing increased 95p latency and occasional OOMs. Mitigated by temporary scale-down + rolling restart of worker replicas.
- Left a short runbook for restart and temporary routing to fallback model variant. Need follow-up PR to adjust memory limits and add a guard for KV cache size (see GH PR linked).

Shift summary:
- Time: 2026-03-03 23:10 UTC - Alert: P95 latency >300ms across region-us-west for model redwood-13b-v2-quant. PagerDuty triggered (INC-4521).
- 23:15 - Observed worker pods in pool-3 with high RSS (1.8GB) and frequent GC spikes. Pod logs show repeated "kv_cache: eviction loop" warnings.
- 23:20 - Decision: divert new requests for redwood-13b-v2-quant to redwood-13b-v2-8bit (lower mem profile) via routing-policy override.
- 23:25 - Performed rolling restart of pool-3: scaled down replicas to 0.5x then back to desired. Latency returned to baseline by 23:40.
- 00:05 - Confirmed no request loss; small increase in error budget used due to reroutes.

Incidents & actions taken (short):
- INC-4521: root cause suspected: runaway KV cache growth on long-conversation sessions + bug in cache eviction.
  - Mitigation: temporary routing to 8bit variant + rolling restart of pool-3.
  - Next steps: add explicit KV cache size guard and alert when per-pod cache > 1GB (see GH PR #1287).

Quick runbook draft - temporary restart procedure (for future oncall):
1) Confirm alert: check metrics in Console -> per-model latency (route: /models/redwood-13b-v2-quant). Check 95p and p99 graphs.
2) Check pods: kubectl -n inference get pods -l pool=pool-3 -o wide
3) Inspect pod logs for "kv_cache" and OOM events: kubectl logs <pod> --since=1h | grep -i kv_cache
4) If multiple pods show evictions/ooms -> perform rolling restart:
   - kubectl -n inference scale deployment pool-3 --replicas=2  # (target smaller than usual to reduce pressure)
   - watch kubectl -n inference get pods -l pool=pool-3 -w
   - once new pods are Ready, scale back to desired replicas: kubectl -n inference scale deployment pool-3 --replicas=6
5) If latency still high after restart -> route traffic to fallback variant via routing override: Console -> Routing -> add temporary rule for model redwood-13b-v2-quant -> redirect to redwood-13b-v2-8bit.
6) Post-incident: add note to incident ticket, attach logs and timeline.

Temporary config/workaround notes:
- Routing override was applied at 23:20 to reroute ~20% traffic initially, then 100% by 23:27 while restart progressed.
- Manual override command (CLI): redwoodctl routing create --model redwood-13b-v2-quant --target redwood-13b-v2-8bit --percentage 100 --expires 1h
- Short-term scaling helped; long-term fix requires memory guard + better KV eviction policy.

Commands & quick checks (cheat sheet):
- Check pods: kubectl -n inference get pods -l pool=pool-3
- Pod logs: kubectl logs <pod> --follow --tail=200
- Restart single pod: kubectl -n inference delete pod <pod>  # deployment will recreate
- View routing rules: redwoodctl routing list --model redwood-13b-v2-quant
- Revert routing: redwoodctl routing delete <routing-id>

Contacts / escalation:
- Primary SRE oncall (today): Marcus Rivera (slack:@marcus, pagerduty:PD-ONCALL-SRE)
- Backend infra: Priya Menon (slack:@priya)
notes: Notes to self: follow up with backend team about KV cache telemetry (per-key size). Put a regression test around long-sequence memory usage. Remind product to re-evaluate default quant variant mapping for latency-sensitive routes.
